newsitem.title: USA: Stocks buoyed by bonds, stronger technology shares.
newsitem.headline: Stocks buoyed by bonds, stronger technology shares.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were slightly higher Thursday, thanks to strength in the bond market and gains in technology shares.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 1.49 points at 5,994.72 after gaining nearly 17 points in early trading.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 11-9 on volume of 270 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The technology-laced Nasdaq Composite index was up 6.37 points at 1,212.60. The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.62 to 566.91.
Bonds reacted positively to several pieces of economic data. The 30-year Treasury bond rose 6/32, which lowered its yield to 6.69 percent from 6.71 percent on Wednesday.
The stock market was quiet, however, as investors and money managers were wary of sticking their necks out ahead of Friday's October employment report and the election on Tuesday.

"The market is assuming that the data tomorrow will not show re-acceleration of the economy. That is being discounted by the market right now so it had better be in line," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

"The amplitude of wage increases also better stay moderate or we are in trouble," he said. "With the Dow at 6,000 and the long bond yield around 6.68, we are discounting a soft landing, no inflation pressures and an extended business cycle."
The market's positive tone was set by strength in the high technology sector, still a favourite of money managers looking for a place to invest.
High techs rallied on a forecast by the Semiconductor Industry Association that chip sales may be pulling out of their year-long slump and could grow 3.5 percent in the fourth quarter.
"That has helped sentiment in the group, especially coming at a time when the group was lagging," one trader said.
Intel Corp. was up 1-3/4 at 108-1/2. Cisco Systems Inc. gained 1-3/8 at 59-1/2.
Metz said the market was unlikely to rally following next Tuesday's elections.
Wall Street is anticipating a victory by President Clinton over Republican challenger Bob Dole and that the Republicans will retain control of both houses of Congress.

"That is what Wall Street wants and if it gets it the market will sell off because it has been anticipated," he said. "If the Democrats carry Congress there will be some short-term concern about the temptation for a new spending binge. Markets will sell off."

In economic news, September personal incomes rose as expected by 0.6 percent compared with a revised 0.5 percent increase in August, while personal spending rose a lower-than-expected 0.1 percent vs. a revised 0.5 percent increase in the previous month.
Starbucks Corp. was down 2 at 33 after the company reported weaker-than-expected sales for October.
Biogen Inc. lost 4 to 74-1/4. The company said it was disappointed with a ruling by Britain's House of Lords dismissing a hepatitis B treatment patent.
